title: Boolean affine refinement compatible with finitely many closed subschemes
statement: Let $X$ be an affine Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning it is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $C_1,\ldots,C_r\hookrightarrow X$ be finitely many closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. There is a finite family of immersions $R_\alpha\hookrightarrow X$ whose images are pairwise disjoint locally closed subsets [def-weil-locally-closed-subset] covering $X$, with every $R_\alpha$ affine and reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], such that for every $\alpha,j$ the pullback $C_j\times_XR_\alpha\to R_\alpha$ [def-pc-fibre-product] has either empty underlying space or underlying space all of $R_\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 095K, label lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, proof: final Noetherian partition paragraph (partition by the finitely many $T_i$ and pairwise intersections)

proof.text: Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$. By the affine characterization of closed immersions, write $C_j=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I_j)$ over $X$, and let $Z_j=V(I_j)$. For $e\in\{0,1\}^r$, set $J_e=\sum_{e_j=1}I_j$, $D_e=\operatorname{Spec}(A/J_e)$, and $U_e=X\setminus\bigcup_{e_j=0}Z_j$. Use $J_e=0$ for an empty sum and $U_e=X$ for an empty union. Set $Y_e=D_e\times_X U_e$. The projection $Y_e\to U_e$ is a closed immersion by closed-immersion base change, and $U_e\to X$ is an open immersion, so $Y_e\to X$ is an immersion. Its image is $B_e=\bigcap_{e_j=1}Z_j\cap\bigcap_{e_j=0}(X\setminus Z_j)$ by the base-change image formula. These subsets are locally closed, pairwise disjoint, and cover $X$, since each point has a unique membership vector. Keep the resulting scheme structure on $Y_e$; no reduction is taken at this stage.

source.place: Tag 095K, proof of lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, final Noetherian partition paragraph: partition by the finitely many T_i and their pairwise intersections

proof.text: By [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], applied to the affine open $X$ of the locally Noetherian scheme $X$ itself, $A$ is Noetherian. Each $A/J_e$ is Noetherian: for an ideal $K\subset A/J_e$, its inverse image in $A$ has finitely many generators by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], whose images generate $K$. Thus $D_e=\operatorname{Spec}(A/J_e)$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth] (the single affine cover), and quasi-compact because it is a closed subspace of the quasi-compact space $X$; given an open cover of that closed subspace, extend the opens to $X$ and add its open complement to obtain a finite subcover. Hence $D_e$ is Noetherian. The scheme $Y_e$ is its open subscheme over $U_e$, so [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] makes $Y_e$ Noetherian. Discard the empty atoms.

source.place: Tag 095K, proof of lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, final Noetherian partition paragraph; affine refinement of the Noetherian partition

proof.text: Apply the finite affine partition lemma to each nonempty Y_e. It gives a finite partition of Y_e by locally closed reduced affine subschemes R_{e,a}. Composing each immersion R_{e,a} -> Y_e with the immersion Y_e -> X gives an immersion into X, by composition stability of immersions. Since the Y_e are pairwise disjoint and cover X, the resulting finite family has pairwise disjoint images and covers X; every source is affine and reduced.

source.place: Tag 095K, proof of lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, final paragraph: refine the finite partition to affine strata

proof.text: Fix a resulting piece R_{e,a}. Its image is contained in B_e. Therefore, for every j, the image is either contained in Z_j (when e_j=1) or disjoint from Z_j (when e_j=0), by the definition of the Boolean atom. This is exactly the required set-theoretic compatibility before passing to the scheme-theoretic pullback.

source.place: Tag 095K, proof of lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, final paragraph: partition so each T_i is either present or absent on a stratum

proof.text: For each j, form the pullback P_{e,a,j}=C_j x_X R_{e,a} -> R_{e,a}. The projection is a closed immersion by stability of closed immersions under base change. Its underlying image is the inverse image in R_{e,a} of the underlying image Z_j of C_j, by the image-of-a-base-change formula. By the preceding step that inverse image is either all of R_{e,a} or empty. Since a closed immersion identifies its source with its image, the underlying space of P_{e,a,j} is respectively all of R_{e,a} or empty.

source.place: Tag 095K, proof of lemma-decompose-quasi-finite-morphism, final Noetherian partition paragraph: each X_j x_X T_i is set-theoretically a union of strata

proof.text: There are finitely many bit vectors and each affine partition is finite, so the resulting family is finite. If X is empty, take the empty family; if r=0, take any finite reduced affine partition from the same construction. All required clauses follow.

split_report.summary: Boolean atoms are formed as open restrictions of explicit closed affine quotient schemes, without reducing the intermediate atoms. Their Noetherianness follows from the existing affine-open lemma, the explicit ideal argument for quotients, and open-subscheme permanence. The closed affine-partition theorem then supplies reduced affine strata. Closed-immersion base change and the base-change image identity prove the required pullback-space condition. No new nodes or statement changes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_noetherian_boolean_affine_refinement {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [CompactSpace X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (r : ℕ) (C : Fin r → Scheme.{u}) (i : ∀ j, C j ⟶ X) [∀ j, IsClosedImmersion (i j)] : ∃ (n : ℕ) (R : Fin n → Scheme.{u}) (ι : ∀ α, R α ⟶ X), (∀ α, IsImmersion (ι α) ∧ IsAffine (R α) ∧ IsReduced (R α) ∧ IsLocallyClosed (Set.range (ι α))) ∧ Pairwise (fun α β : Fin n ↦ Disjoint (Set.range (ι α)) (Set.range (ι β))) ∧ (∀ x : X, ∃ α, x ∈ Set.range (ι α)) ∧ ∀ (α : Fin n) (j : Fin r), Set.range (pullback.snd (i j) (ι α)) = ∅ ∨ Set.range (pullback.snd (i j) (ι α)) = Set.univ
